micro_flaws.core_summary: Missing comparisons with more recent flow-based generative models (e.g., OT-Flow, OTFM) and lacking fair comparisons in terms of compute (parameters, FLOPs, training time).

raw_arguments.Human_4: Placing the number of parameters and the number of parameter updates (or training time on identical hardware) for each model in Table 1 is very important as using an equal number of parameters/compute is essential for ensuring a fair comparison.

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 3. Applicability, Scalability & Limitations - Lack of Discussion on Limitations
micro_flaws.core_summary: The limitations of the method, beyond the ~10% performance gap to diffusion SOTA, are not thoroughly discussed.

raw_arguments.Human_2: Are there more limitations other than the 10% worse than diffusion SOTA?

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 4. Experimental Design & Evaluation - Insufficient Experimental Validation
micro_flaws.core_summary: Several key design choices (e.g., Adaptive Double Normalization, linear warm-up) lack direct experimental ablation or comparative analysis to support their effectiveness.

raw_arguments.Human_3: Similarly, in Section 4.2, the authors propose training with linear warm-up w.r.t the model's time derivative, yet no evidence is provided to demonstrate this choice’s effectiveness.
raw_arguments.Human_5: There are no ablation study results on “Adaptive Double Normalization” except for claiming it “removes its instability in CM training”.

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 6. Methodology & Theoretical Soundness - Lack of Intuition/Justification
micro_flaws.core_summary: The paper lacks intuitive explanations for core components, such as the training loss and the behavior of the adaptive weighting scheme.

raw_arguments.Human_4: The paper would be improved if an intuitive explanation is given for the loss in Equation 2.
raw_arguments.Human_5: In Figure 5b, it looks like “w/o adaptive weighting” achieves better two-step FIDs than “w/ adaptive weighting” and very similar one-step FIDs to “w/ adaptive weighting”. Why do we need adaptive weighting?

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 2. Clarity & Presentation - General writing & Clarity issues
micro_flaws.core_summary: The section on positional embeddings (time embeddings) lacks detail and is not self-contained, requiring external references to understand.

raw_arguments.Human_2: The section on positional embeddings (line 269 and on) lacks details to be fully understandable without having to read another paper. Maybe beefing up that section would make the paper more self-contained.

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 4. Experimental Design & Evaluation - Insufficient Experimental Validation
micro_flaws.core_summary: The paper does not provide a direct comparison of training efficiency (convergence speed, memory cost) between the proposed continuous-time models and previous discrete-time consistency models (ECMs).

raw_arguments.Human_5: Although I really like the improvements of continuous-time consistency models, which could fundamentally eliminate the discretization error in discrete-time consistency models, it comes with more time and memory costs related to JVP computation in the loss function. To this end, this work introduces JVP of Flash Attention to reduce the costs, which is great. Still, there may be a considerable gap between the continuous-time and discrete-time consistency models. I wonder if the paper can provide a more detailed comparison between sCMs and the previous discrete-time consistency models - ECMs, in terms of the training convergence and memory cost.

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 6. Methodology & Theoretical Soundness - Lack of Intuition/Justification
micro_flaws.core_summary: The paper does not explain the intuition behind the discrepancy in sCT vs. sCD performance across different resolutions (especially the increased variance at larger scales).

raw_arguments.Human_1: I am curious about the authors' thoughts on the extent to which the increased variance could be caused by the pretrained image encoder/decoder.
raw_arguments.Human_3: In Figure 6(a) and Section 5.2, the authors mention that sCT is less effective at higher resolutions. Do the authors have any insights into why this might be?
raw_arguments.Human_5: There is no explanation for the phenomenon that sCT performs better than sCD on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-64, but sCTs performs worse on ImageNet-512. Any intuition of why sCT suffers from increased variance at larger scales?

micro_flaws.core_summary: Figure 3 is considered not to add much value by one reviewer.

raw_arguments.Human_2: I found all figure very useful with the exception of Figure (3) which I felt did not add much value.

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 4. Experimental Design & Evaluation - Insufficient Experimental Validation
micro_flaws.core_summary: The evaluation of the adaptive weighting in a two-step generation setting is questioned, as it appears to hurt performance in that regime.

raw_arguments.Human_3: Figure 5(b) suggests that incorporating adaptive weighting in a two-step setting may lead to worse performance, while in the one-step setting, it only yields marginal improvement. Have the authors considered alternative designs for the two step case?

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 5. Related work & Citations - Missing Comparisons with Prior Work
micro_flaws.core_summary: The paper lacks comparisons with recent related works that also improve flow-based models, and with VSD when using TTUR (Two Time-scale Update Rule).

raw_arguments.Human_5: In Figure 7, sCDs condition the consistency network on the guidance scale $s$. I wonder if VSD also condition the generator on the guidance scale, for a consistent evaluation setting?

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 4. Experimental Design & Evaluation - Questionable Evaluation Metrics
micro_flaws.core_summary: The comparison between discrete-time and continuous-time consistency models in Figure 5c may be unfair due to the treatment of timestep scheduling for discrete models.

raw_arguments.Human_5: In Figure 5c, do discrete-time CMs have a constant number of time steps $N$ or a timestep schedule up to the maximum number of steps $N$? If it is the former one, it seems to be a bit unfair to discrete-time CMs because the scheduling of time steps is very important to them. Does it make more sense to compare with the best-performing discrete-time CMs?

micro_flaws.core_summary: Notation inconsistencies and potential errors in equations/lines, such as the reuse of f_θ with different meanings and a possible mistake in c_skip/c_out definitions.

raw_arguments.Human_1: In Line 213 and in Line 227, both diffusion models and consistency models are denoted as $f_	heta(\mathbf{x}_t, t)$ but with different equations.
raw_arguments.Human_4: Shouldn't $c_{skip}$ and $c_{out}$ be $\sigma_t$ and  $ \alpha_t \sigma_d$, that is for $\sigma_t=t$ and  $\alpha_t=1$: $c_{skip}=t$  and $c_{out}=\sigma_d$ in line 201/202?
raw_arguments.Human_5: A minor issue: In line 266, should it be $c_{\text{noise}}(t) = \frac{1}{4} \log(\sigma_d \tan t) $?

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 2. Clarity & Presentation - General writing & Clarity issues
micro_flaws.core_summary: The explanation of the 'Adaptive Double Normalization' technique is insufficient, leaving it unclear if it's the same as local response normalization.

raw_arguments.Human_1: The Adaptive Double Normalization is less explained. Is it the same as local response normalization applied to the modulation layer?

micro_flaws.core_summary: The paper does not discuss or demonstrate applicability to text-to-image generation, which is a key application area for modern generative models.

raw_arguments.Human_3: Additionally, given that the model is trained on a large-scale dataset (ImageNet 512) under latent setting, it would be beneficial to include discussions related to text-to-image generation.

micro_flaws.core_summary: Potential typos and errors in the math/text are noted, including incorrect squaring, a variable not depending on time as claimed, and inconsistencies in appendix equations.

raw_arguments.Human_4: The paragraph from line 924 to 938 (appendix) needs additional elaboration regarding the implications of having $||(\alpha_t, \sigma_t)||=1$ with respect to the invariance of the geometric set connecting $x_0$ and $z$.
